(B) The 4 single-family districts (RE, RT, RS, RM) were replaced 2026-09-07 with data from Georgetown's adopted-but-not-yet-effective UDC rewrite (City Council adopted 2026-08-11; effective 2026-11-01 per rewrite Section 1.09) -- these are primary-source-verified against the rewrite PDF, not against the real code-section atom corpus, because that corpus only contains the CURRENTLY-in-force (pre-rewrite) text (confirmed live: zero real atoms mention the rewrite's new district name 'Residential Traditional', while several mention the pre-rewrite name 'Residential Low Density') -- there is nothing in the real corpus to round-trip rewrite text against. FOLLOW-UP NEEDED (not done here): once the rewrite is closer to taking effect or after 2026-11-01, the other 9 districts need the same post-rewrite research the 4 SF ones just got, or this table carries two vintages indefinitely. See each district's own provenance for adopted_date/effective_date/pre_rewrite_value_verified fields marking which vintage a given value belongs to. --- ORIGINAL NOTE (districts TF/TH/MF-1/MF-2/CN/C-1/C-3/OF/IN, current code): Codified from the City of Georgetown Unified Development Code (UDC), Chapter 6 (Residential Development Standards) Section 6.02 and Chapter 7 (Non-Residential Development Standards) Table 7.02.020 — Supplement 15, codified through Ordinance No. 2025-54 adopted September 9, 2025 (Municode ProductID 13943, job Id 480427). Source is Municode; each district cites its own Section 6.02.0x0 (residential) or the shared Table 7.02.020 (non-residential) deep-link. PENDING REWRITE CAVEAT: Georgetown's UDC is mid-rewrite with an updated version expected ~mid-2026; this table pins the CURRENT IN-FORCE edition (Supp. 15 / Ord. 2025-54) and MUST be re-verified when the rewrite lands. MODELING NOTES: (1) The Georgetown UDC dimensional tables state 'Impervious Cover, maximum %: See Section 11.02' (residential) / 'Impervious coverage: Refer to Section 11.02' (non-residential) and state NO per-district building lot-coverage cap, so both max_impervious_pct and max_lot_coverage_pct are flagged not_specified in provenance and carry 100 as a non-binding stand-in (the envelope draw uses setbacks, not these fields). (2) The UDC's corner/street-facing value is 'Side/Rear Street Setback' — codified as side_corner_ft. (3) Residential 'Side Setback' is the base interior side; the MF-1/MF-2 larger side/rear values are the setback-to-residential-district figures and are NOT used as the base side_ft (base interior side is codified). (4) TH (Townhouse) side_ft uses the 'Non-shared Wall Side Setback' (10 ft); the shared-wall side is 0. (5) Non-residential districts (CN/C-1/C-3/OF/BP/IN/PF) draw from the single shared Table 7.02.020; side_ft is the base 'Side setback, min.' and side_corner_ft mirrors that base where the table states no distinct corner value (non-res table has no separate street-side column, so side_corner_ft = side_ft, flagged). (6) AG (Agriculture) and MU-DT/MU (form-based, 'See Section 4.09') are EXCLUDED — no simple per-district front/side/rear setback table. See the addendum.] --- REWRITE RESEARCH NOTE (districts RE/RT/RS/RM, effective 2026-11-01): IMPORTANT TIMING CAVEAT: Georgetown's original UDC (adopted 2003-03-11, in force today) is being wholesale replaced. City Council adopted a full UDC rewrite on 2026-08-11; per UDC Section 1.09 the rewrite becomes effective 2026-11-01. This file is coded from the REWRITE text (City of Georgetown, 'Unified Development Code 2026', PDF published at https://cms3.revize.com/revize/georgetowntx/Documents/Development%20Services/Planning/Unified%20Development%20Code/UDC%20Rewrite%20Draft%20Content/Unified%20Development%20Code%208.11.2026.pdf, accessed 2026-09-06), NOT from the pre-rewrite code that is the only code legally in force between now and 2026-10-31. The rewrite's own Section 4.02 'Zoning District Equivalency Table' confirms these are direct successors of the pre-rewrite districts, same short codes, same lineage: pre-rewrite 'RE Residential Estate'->RE (unchanged), 'RL Residential Low Density'->RT Residential Traditional, 'RS Residential Single-family'->RS Residential Suburban, 'TF Two-family'/'TH Townhouse'->RM Residential Mix. Max building height for RS is independently cross-checked at 35 ft under BOTH codes via a City of Georgetown Planning Department staff report (Sofia Nelson, Planning Director; City Council item, 2026-01-14, https://d2kbkoa27fdvtw.cloudfront.net/georgetown/e60a6c7d2d185c1f926d7bba471eb3350.pdf, 'Current UDC' height table, RS = 35'), which is the only pre-rewrite dimensional figure this pass could independently verify -- the pre-rewrite code's front/side/rear/corner setback and impervious-cover numbers could NOT be verified (see confidence report; Municode's current-UDC pages at https://library.municode.com/tx/georgetown/codes/unified_development_code render client-side via an Angular SPA that returned only an empty app shell to every fetch method available this session, including a browser-UA curl GET (HTTP 200, 6KB shell, zero table content) and the Wayback Machine's historical crawls of the same URL pattern (all captures 1.8-3.3KB, same shell, per CDX API query), so no pre-rewrite chapter text was retrievable this session). SCOPE: covers the rewrite's four Chapter 7 residential districts whose descriptions explicitly allow single-family detached and/or attached housing -- RE Residential Estate (Sec. 7.02.030), RT Residential Traditional (Sec. 7.02.040), RS Residential Suburban (Sec. 7.02.050, the City's standard single-family-detached district and the direct successor to pre-rewrite 'RS'), and RM Residential Mix (Sec. 7.02.060, allows single-family detached/attached alongside duplex/townhouse). OMITTED as out of scope for a single-family corpus: AG Agriculture, MF-1/MF-2 multifamily, MH Manufactured Housing, all non-residential and overlay districts, and all ETJ-specific standards. [P-258 lane-c, 2026-09-16: SUPERSEDED IN PART — AG, MH, PF and MU-DT now have rows in this file from the adopted 2026 rewrite (effective 2026-11-01); MF-1/MF-2 and the overlay/ETJ standards remain unrowed.] Where a district's Chapter 7 table splits values by garage/parking access (front-loaded vs. alley-loaded lots), this file reports the front-loaded ('front-access') column as the canonical row, since front-loaded is the default/majority lot configuration; alley-loaded variants are captured in each field's provenance quote and are NOT separately rowed (schema is one row per district). Georgetown's 2026 code has no 'lot coverage' concept distinct from impervious cover (full-text search for 'lot coverage'/'building coverage' in the 501-page rewrite returned zero hits) -- max_lot_coverage_pct uses the same non-binding sentinel-100 convention established in this corpus's pflugerville-tx.json for a genuinely absent metric. max_impervious_pct values for RE and RT carry lower confidence: Table 13.02.010-2 (p.320) labels every row with a 'front-access'/'alley-access' qualifier, but RE's and RT's own Chapter 7 dimensional tables have no alley-loaded lot type at all, so the qualifier attached to their single impervious-cover row in Table 13.02.010-2 is very likely a pdftotext column-bleed artifact from the neighboring RS/RM rows -- the numeric value (RE 20%, RT 40%) is transcribed exactly as printed and directly adjacent to the correct district name, but the access-type label should not be trusted. See per-field provenance for full detail and the accompanying sourcing/confidence note delivered alongside this file. P-258 LANE-C ADDENDUM (2026-09-16, acquisition campaign, branch seat/p258-lane-c): 4 districts added, plus the RL contradiction that P-225 left behind is now RESOLVED IN WRITING below. VINTAGE, STATED PLAINLY: Georgetown's UDC is mid-rewrite. The existing single-family rows (RE/RT/RS/RM) are already coded from the adopted rewrite (City Council adopted 2026-08-11; effective 2026-11-01 per rewrite Section 1.09); the 9 non-single-family rows (TF/TH/MF-1/MF-2/CN/C-1/C-3/OF/IN) are still coded from the pre-rewrite code (Supp. 15 / Ord. 2025-54). The 4 rows added here (AG, MH, PF, MU-DT) are coded from the SAME REWRITE PDF as the existing RE/RT/RS/RM rows -- 'Unified Development Code 2026', https://cms3.revize.com/revize/georgetowntx/Documents/Development%20Services/Planning/Unified%20Development%20Code/UDC%20Rewrite%20Draft%20Content/Unified%20Development%20Code%208.11.2026.pdf -- and every added value carries adopted_date 2026-08-11 / effective_date 2026-11-01 / pre_rewrite_value_verified: false in its provenance, exactly like the rows already there. They are therefore NOT in force between 2026-09-16 and 2026-10-31; they are the adopted, imminent text. Read the four rows as 'what this district will be', not 'what it is today'. ADDED: AG Agriculture (Section 7.02.020.A, the rewrite's initial default zoning for annexed land), MH Manufactured Housing (7.02.090.A), PF Public Facilities (8.02.050.A), MU-DT Mixed-Use Downtown (4.05.040.B). IMPERSHABLE COVER, READ NOT ASSUMED: AG 20% from Table 13.02.010-2 and PF 70% from Table 13.02.010-1, both real ordinance figures. MH and MU-DT get the not_specified 100 sentinel because their sections say only 'Maximum impervious cover: See Section 13.02' AND their district names appear in neither Table 13.02.010-1 nor Table 13.02.010-2 -- that is a documented absence, not a copy from a neighbour. max_lot_coverage_pct stays the established sentinel-100/not_specified convention on all four (the rewrite has no lot-coverage concept distinct from impervious cover; full-text search for 'lot coverage'/'building coverage' returns zero hits). THE REWRITE'S 'Street-facing garage setback' ROW (25 ft in AG, RE, RT and MH) IS NOT CODIFIED AS A YARD SETBACK: it is a garage-placement line, not a front/side/rear yard minimum, so it is deliberately NOT substituted into front_ft (the comma-separated 'Front/primary street setback' row is the front yard). === RL CONTRADICTION RESOLVED (P-225 leave-behind) === THE COMMENT IS WRONG AS WRITTEN. lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/zoning-layers.ts:22 claimed 'Verified live 2026-07-20 for all 12 setback districts (RE/RL/RS/TF/TH/MF-1/MF-2/CN/C-1/C-3/OF/IN)'. RL has never had a row in this table (the single-family rows are RE/RT/RS/RM), and the current rewrite lists RL in NEITHER its district roster (AG/RE/RT/RS/RM/MF-1/MF-2/MH/CN/C-1/C-2/PF/I-1/I-2/PUD/MU-DT) nor its Chapter 7 or Chapter 8 dimensional standards. The rewrite's Section 4.02 Equivalency Table (Table 4.01.010-1) maps previous-UDC 'RL Residential Low Density' -> current-UDC 'RT Residential Traditional', which is why the successor RT row exists and why a live district-list check can be misread as 'RL covered'. EVIDENCE: rewrite Table 4.01.010-1 (read this pass from the PDF above) plus the absence of any RL section in the rewrite's 7.02/8.02 chapter listings. CONSEQUENCE AND FIX: a parcel stamped 'RL' by the Georgetown zoning layer normalizes to 'RL' and matches NO row's leading token (the RT row normalizes to 'RT'), so it correctly falls to the conservative fallback rather than being mis-matched; the comment's claim that RL was verified as covered is nonetheless false and the comment has been corrected in the same commit. The worklist carries RL at 50 parcels; P-225's live re-check reported 3 parcels on the same code. Either way the code is real in the stamped layer and has no dimensional table of its own: it is a SUPERSEDED pre-rewrite district whose successor (RT) is already rowed, so a separate RL row would assert the successor's numbers under the predecessor's name -- exactly the silent pick the campaign forbids. RL is therefore recorded as BLOCKED with the equivalency cited, not rowed. === BP (Business Park), 23 parcels, ALSO NOT ROWED AND FOR A RELATED REASON === Rewrite Section 4.02.B declares the Two-Family, Townhouse, Office, Business Park and Industrial districts LEGACY ZONING DISTRICTS, and Section 4.02.C says property in a legacy zoning district 'shall continue to be subject to zoning regulations applicable at the time the property was rezoned to a legacy zoning district'. The rewrite's Table 4.01.010-1 shows BP Business Park -> I-1 Flex Industrial prospectively, but the DIMENSIONAL text that still governs an existing BP parcel is the pre-rewrite code's, and no pre-rewrite dimensional text was retrievable this pass (Municode's Georgetown UDC renders client-side in an Angular SPA that returned only an empty app shell to every fetch method, including a browser-UA GET (HTTP 200, ~6KB shell, zero table content) and the Wayback Machine's captures of the same URL pattern (all captures 1.8-3.3KB, same shell, per CDX API query)). BP is recorded BLOCKED with those sources named; the I-1 row is NOT substituted because I-1 governs only from 2026-11-01 and only for property rezoned after adoption. === CONFLICT FOUND IN THIS FILE'S OWN EXISTING DATA (reported, NOT silently edited) === Table 13.02.010-2 as read this pass prints 'AG Agriculture 20%', 'RE Residential Estate 40%', 'RT Residential Transition 40%'. The pre-existing RE row in this file carries max_impervious_pct 20 (i.e. the value this pass reads for AG) while RT carries 40. This file's own note already warns that RE's and RT's impervious values were suspected of a column-bleed/row-shift artifact. This pass's read is evidence that the RE row is shifted by one: RE should be 40 and 20 belongs to AG. The RE and RT rows were left UNTOUCHED (they belong to another lane's work and a single-pass read is not sufficient to rewrite an existing verified value); they are flagged here and in the lane-c self-report so the owner can re-read Table 13.02.010-2 against a second rendering before correcting. The AG row added here takes 20% from the same table, which is consistent with (not dependent on) that finding. SOURCES TRIED for the Georgetown units still uncoded after this pass (RL, BP): Municipal Code Corporation/Municode (Angular SPA shell, HTTP 200, no server-rendered text -- multiple methods), the Wayback Machine (all captures shells), the City's revize/cms3 document centre (the adopted 2026 rewrite PDF -- read in full, which is how the RL equivalency and the BP legacy declaration were established), and the rewrite's own Table 4.01.010-1 equivalency table (read). side_corner_ft.quote: MU-DT, Lot and Dimensional Standards: the table states NO separate corner-side/secondary-street column (rows are front/primary street 0, build-to option, side 0, rear 0), so side_corner_ft mirrors the side setback 0 and is flagged as a mirror rather than a distinct tabulated value.

max_height_ft.quote: MU-DT, Lot and Dimensional Standards, row F: 'Building height, maximum feet: 40' (footnote 3: stadium structures/lighting/scoreboards exempted but set back a minimum of 120 ft).

max_lot_coverage_pct.quote: undefined (P-258 lane-c, 2026-09-16: `confidence` added — the four rows this pass added carried the field without it, which is a rule-G6 block.)

max_impervious_pct.quote: MU-DT's own table says only 'Maximum impervious cover: See Section 13.02', and MU-DT appears in NEITHER Table 13.02.010-1 (non-residential districts: CN/C-1/C-2/PF/I-1/I-2) NOR Table 13.02.010-2 (residential: AG/RE/RT/RS/RM/MF-1/MF-2). No district figure is stated for MU-DT -- 100 is the established non-binding sentinel and must be treated as not_specified.
